verdict.headline: Bond market eases for first time in two weeks; S&P futures hold flat after record
verdict.label: Post-record consolidation; 30Y drifts toward 5.19%; AMD and AMAT China signal in focus
verdict.rationale_short: The 30Y has compressed pre-market to approximately 5.19% — the first meaningful move in the long end after CPI core 2.5% and PPI flat — but still 4bps above the 5.15% threshold needed to relieve growth-multiple pressure. September hike odds hold at ~33%. The session's two reads: whether today's 30Y close sustains the compression, and whether AMD's open reveals that AMAT's China equipment-demand signal is extending beyond capital goods to chip designers. If the 30Y reclaims 5.24% on no catalyst, Jackson Hole remains the only venue to move the long end before August 26.

trade_setups.thesis: The pre-market compression to ~5.19% is the first meaningful move in the long end after two consecutive below-consensus inflation prints. Whether it holds through Friday's close is the session's primary test. Two consecutive closes at or below 5.18% before August 26 would be the first concrete evidence the soft-data trajectory is working on the long end ahead of Jackson Hole.
trade_setups.entry: Levels that define it: 5.20% close confirms compression is holding. 5.23% bounce on no catalyst confirms the bond market is holding its prior against the soft-data read.
trade_setups.invalidation: 30Y above 5.28% post-Jackson Hole reinstates the rate overhang entering September 18 FOMC.

trade_setups.thesis: AMAT's earnings decline surfaced a China equipment demand component that may extend to chip designers. AMD closed as the sole semiconductor decliner in the record August 13 session. AMD has meaningful China data-center revenue. The altitude-plus-China thesis is forming around AMD; the August 14 open relative to $478 and $484 is the session's first real-time read on how far the signal has traveled.
trade_setups.entry: Levels that define it: open below $478 = China read extends to chip designers; hold above $484 on two closes post-AMAT = equipment-specific containment; break below $475 on volume = broader semiconductor spread confirmed.
trade_setups.invalidation: AMD holds above $484 on two consecutive sessions after AMAT's result, with no new China-specific negative catalyst.

trade_setups.thesis: S&P 500 inclusion effective August 18 drives mechanical passive demand. RDDT at ~$177 pre-market (+12%) reflects index mechanics, not a fundamental re-rating of Reddit's advertising durability in an AI-search environment. Peak buying concentrates at the August 17 closing auction. Post-mechanics, RDDT reverts to its own fundamental case.
trade_setups.entry: Mechanical demand peaks August 17 close. Two sessions of RDDT holding above ~$177 post-August 18 tests whether the fundamental bid supports the mechanical bid.
trade_setups.invalidation: RDDT reverses below its inclusion-announcement close (~$158) within two sessions of August 18.

bear_case: The 30Y pre-market compression to 5.19% required two consecutive below-consensus inflation prints and an entire week to deliver 5bps of relief — a rate that would take months to close the remaining gap to 5.00%. The bond market retains its structural prior: 3.4% annual CPI, SPR at 40-year lows, and Iran's stated conditions (sanction relief, war reparations) remain formally unmet. If August 14's session produces a 30Y bounce above 5.23% on no catalyst, the long end is explicitly holding its prior and the path to 5.15% is on Warsh's keynote alone. September hike odds at 33% are asymmetrically positioned: from 33%, a speech that validates 30Y persistence at current levels has significantly more room to move odds upward than a soft speech has to move them lower. That read no longer holds if the 30Y closes below 5.15% on two consecutive sessions before August 26.
